Whole image viewed once; half a once; half b once, in that order. Eleven crops were created with LANCZOS enlargement to width 2800, autocontrast and light sharpening, and each crop was displayed once. No whole or half was redisplayed. No OCR, web, other pages or other readers were used.

hua_has=text. H supplies a main-text summary, not a diplomatic transcript, plus transcribed marginal annotations. Main-text absence is recorded by coherent blocks; the summary’s paraphrases are not treated as literal readings. H is present, not absent.

Manuscript page IX appears at the upper right with upper and lower rules. Archive pencil sheet number 35 is at the lower left and appears only as a comment in reading.tex. No date or page count is visible. The page names Lemme XI.

The fair-copy prose is dark ink. Darker, thicker marginal corrections and lighter pencil annotations are distinguished descriptively; no named person is inferred from handwriting or catalog. The side-count insertion and OPS line look lighter than the fair copy, while the inequality is darkened; material/hand assignment is not forensic.

The opening continuation argues for an interior angle below pi via a convex polygon and exterior angular sectors, then says a convex polygon has at least three vertices. Lemme XI asserts two vertices of a J-polygone visible from one another from the interior, with an added side count. Its proof starts with a chosen s, its two neighbors, and their triangle, and discusses a first empty-intersection case and a second intersection-on-the-base case.
The adjacent annotation says “faux pour n=3!”. This makes strict > tempting, but the overwritten lower branch remains ambiguous; ≥ was retained as an alternative.

The same tall-stem oval appears after = and != in intersection formulas, suggesting an empty-set role. The transcription nonetheless follows its phi-shaped strokes and marks phi/varnothing at the first occurrence.

The subsequent claims about a vertex on ]s′,s″[ and empty interior intersection are consistent with a containment reading. No formula was emended on this ground: the crop itself shows an intact subset and a detached diagonal hooked leader. No proof of those claims was attempted.
The argument refers to an interior intersection, but that does not establish the earlier overwritten word. Final int is clear and the earlier ext remains marked uncertain.
